newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-RODRIGUEZ SLAM KEEPS EXPOS' HOPES ALIVE.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-RODRIGUEZ SLAM KEEPS EXPOS' HOPES ALIVE.

text.p: Henry Rodriguez hit a grand slam as the Montreal Expos kept their wild-card hopes alive with a 5-2 win over the Philadelphia Phillies Thursday.
Montreal moved within one game of idle San Diego for the National League wild-card berth. The Expos conclude their season with a three-game series at home against Atlanta.
"We still got a chance," said Rodriguez. "We're going to try and win all the games because we can't afford to lose one."
Rodriguez's 36th homer of the season made him the seventh Expo ever to get 100 RBI and the first since Tim Wallach had 123 in 1987. It was Rodriguez's first career grand slam.
"I was just trying to hit a fly ball, to make contact and get a sacrifice fly," said Rodriguez. "I hit it pretty good, but I never thought it would go out. Hitting a grand slam is great.
It was the ninth grand slam of the season for Montreal, tying a National League record set by the 1929 Cubs and the 1995 Padres.

Omar Daal (4-5) allowed two runs over five innings with five hits, a walk and seven strikeouts. Dave Veres and Ugueth Urbina combined to allow two hits in three scoreless innings and Mel Rojas pitched the ninth for his 35th save. Rojas has converted 27 straight save opportunities, a club record.
Curt Schilling (9-10) allowed five runs and five hits with two walks and 11 strikeouts in seven innings. It was his eighth start this season with 10 strikeouts.

In Los Angeles, Mark Gardner pitched a seven-hitter for his fourth complete game and the San Francisco Giants prevented the Dodgers from clinching at least a tie for the N.L. West title with a 6-1 victory.
The loss trimmed the Dodgers' lead over second-place San Diego to two games. Los Angeles hosts the Padres in a three-game showdown beginning Friday.
Gardner (12-7) walked none and struck out seven. Tom Candiotti (9-11) took the loss.
Bill Mueller, Willie Delgado and Glenallen Hill each had two hits and an RBI for the Giants.
At Florida, Al Leiter tossed a six-hitter for his 16th win and Jeff Conine added a three-run homer as the Marlins won their sixth straight game, 7-1 over the Atlanta Braves.
Leiter (16-12) tossed his second complete game of the season, the other coming in his no-hitter in May against Colorado. He walked three and struck out eight.
He struck out Andruw Jones and Eddie Perez to end the game and finish the season with 200 strikeouts.
"The most K's I ever had was 153. In the ninth inning I wanted those two strikeouts," Leiter said. "But they were hacking and making first-pitch outs.
"I kept thinking, how am I going to get two strikes on these guys so I can strike them out? But I struck out the last two guys. This is an unbelievable way to end the season."
The Marlins got three hits and an RBI from Andre Dawson, who is closing out an illustrious career.
"It was good to finish up that way," said Dawson, who received a standing ovation.
Atlanta starter Denny Neagle (16-9) allowed seven runs and nine hits in 4 2/3 innings, walking three and striking out seven.
Neagle, who has struggled since being acquired by the N.L. East winners on August 28, may have jeopardised his position as Atlanta's fourth starter in the playoffs.
"I got it out of my system for the playoffs," Neagle said.
"I made stupid pitches. I didn't use my head out there."
In Houston, Derek Bell's two-run single snapped a seventh-inning tie and Doug Drabek allowed two runs over seven innings as the Astros defeated the New York Mets 6-2.

Lance Johnson had his 21st triple, the most by a National League player since Adam Comorosky hit 23 for the Pirates in 1930. Johnson, who went 3-for-4, has 225 hits, the most in the N.L. since Matty Alou had 231 for Pittsburgh in 1969.

"This has been a good year for me," Johnson said. "Most of the time, I feel very comfortable at the plate. Most of the time, I'm just spraying the ball like I usually do. After the season, I'll sit back and look at the records."

In Cincinnati, Hal Morris extended his hitting streak to 26 games by driving in a pair of runs with a single in a three-run second inning and Willie Greene hit his fifth homer in three games as the Reds beat the Chicago Cubs 12-4.

Morris's hitting streak is one game short of Padre John Flahery's season-best and is the fourth-longest in club history -- behind Pete Rose's 44-game skein in 1978 and the 27-game runs of Vada Pinson in 1965 and Edd Roush in 1920 and 1924.
